articles.title: What Do We Mean When We Say 'F*ck AI'?: Moral Panic, Semantic Indeterminacy, and the Reification of Techno-Capitalism
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.05574v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Academic and (increasingly) public resistance to artificial intelligence (AI) often blurs the line between legitimate critique of techno-capitalist exploitation and (inflated) existential risk. Moreover, discourse around AI can sometimes resemble a "moral panic" where an apparently clear and identifiable scapegoat is targeted in lieu of the complex systemic problems that are causing (genuine and justified) social anxieties. articles.title: Cibersapiens: Gamifying Cybersecurity Education to Engage Secondary Students
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.05587v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cybersecurity education and awareness are often tailored for businesses, leaving general citizens, especially young people, unprepared. Despite the availability of educational resources, cybersecurity training is not provided equally to all individuals, particularly children and teenagers. As digital risks such as sexting, grooming, and cyberbullying, among others, increase, young users remain vulnerable. articles.title: The Male Abstraction Bias in Internet Culture and Large Language Models
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.05730v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two foundational aspects of human cognition, abstractness and gender, are typically examined as separable. articles.title: Thick Alignment: A Social Framework for Values and AI Systems
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.05857v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Computer science research on the "alignment" of artificial intelligence (AI) systems treats human values as content to be specified and optimized. Decades of social science scholarship describe values differently, as enacted in ordinary practice, interpreted in social context, and contested across plural orders of evaluation and worth. articles.title: Who Gets Counted? Large Language Models, Informative Refusal, and Downstream Bias in Name-Based Demographic Classification
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.06550v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Researchers routinely infer gender, race, and ethnicity from names, yet the standard tools used for this task misclassify the groups that diversity research most needs to measure. Large language models (LLMs) have been proposed as a remedy because they label diverse names accurately. We ask whether that accuracy carries over to the estimates researchers report. articles.title: Does Personality Persuade? Investigating Personality Trait Prompting and Persuasion in Large Language Models
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.06572v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can be prompted to express different personality profiles, but it remains unclear how reliably they do so or whether personality affects their persuasiveness. articles.summary: arXiv:2611.06709v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Responsible AI scholarship has found that ethical principles are frequently not reflected in AI design and development.
